terms.gloss: usually, as a rule, for the most part
evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam
Cic. Off. 1.135: habentur autem plērumque sermōnēs aut dē domesticīs negōtiīs aut dē rē pūblicā
terms.comment: In Cicero “as a rule, mostly”; in Tacitus and later often no more than “often” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: usually do, be in the habit of
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, semi-deponent, with an infinitive
evidence: Cic. Off. 3.59: sed hīc piscārī nūllī solent
Ov. Fast. 4.170: quae septem dīcī, sex tamen esse solent
terms.comment: Latin says “usually” as often with this verb as with an adverb; ut solet, as usual (see as usual).

terms.gloss: as a rule, usually; with numbers, about
evidence: Ter. Ph. 363–364: rūrī ferē sē continēbat
Sen. Ep. 53.1: quae ferē aut in aquam aut in ventum resolvuntur
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “in the usual course of things”, as against interdum or rārō; ut ferē fit, as usually happens (Cic. Inv. 2.14).

phrases.latin: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō
phrases.english: I wake when I like: usually about the first hour, often before, rarely later

phrases.latin: pauper, cui opera vīta erat, rūrī ferē sē continēbat
phrases.english: being poor, with only his work to live on, he usually kept to the country

sources: Lewis & Short: plerusque (plērumque) · Lewis & Short: soleo · Lewis & Short: fere
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 401.
